text:
marcus: Quick report from a new user onboarding — their sample app started hitting the wrong tenant when they set REDWOOD_API_KEY + REDWOOD_PROJECT. they expected env var to win.

anya: can you paste the log snippet / repro?
marcus: repro:
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_user_zzz
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme-team
start sample app `rw start`
logs: "env key used: pk_user_zzz" then "resolved project metadata -> org default pk_org_fallback" and traffic goes to org tenant.

oscar: that smells like our auth resolver calls project metadata early and overwrites the env key. should never replace an explicit credential.

anya: checking code: auth/chain.ts currently does: if (REDWOOD_PROJECT) use ProjectProvider else chain envVar -> file -> metadata. so project path short-circuits. oops.

sophie: oof. that explains several support tickets last week where users reported being routed to company org even though they config'd env key.

infra-bot: created issue INF-870: project-provider should not override explicit credentials. linked to PR template.

marcus: short-term mitigation idea: when starting sample apps in docs, recommend using `REDWOOD_PROJECT` only for team-managed CI, and for local dev prefer project-less env. also add a note in onboarding.

oscar: long-term: change resolver precedence to: CLI flag > env var > config file > project metadata/org default. and add unit tests for: env var preserved, flag overrides, project lookup only when no explicit creds.

anya: i'll draft PR. also adding an audit log event when resolver falls back to org default so support can detect silent overrides (telemetry + a visible warning when run locally).

sophie: can we also detect when the env key and resolved org key are from different tenants and warn the user? helpful for rotation cases where old keys linger.

marcus: yes please. case I saw was a rotated project key in metadata pointing to new org default, while the dev had an older env key — mismatch caused confusing 403s.

infra-bot: PR opened anya/fix-auth-order #901. CI: 4 checks queued.

anya: PR will: change precedence, add tests, emit a single-line console warning when an implicit override would occur, and add `rw auth:whoami` that prints provider source. leaving verbose off by default.

oscar: sounds good. can you also include migration note for on-call and update sampleapp README? that onboarding doc needs a short FAQ about env vs project.

sophie: adding a support playbook note: if onboarding user sees unexpected tenant, ask for `rw auth:whoami --json` output and advise unset REDWOOD_PROJECT while debugging.

marcus: awesome — thanks. this should stop more confused new users. :raised_hands:
